​Sandy (Presentation & Communication Lead): The voice and presenter of the team, responsible for showcasing the project, storytelling, and delivering the mission vision to the audience.
summary:
Space Journey is an interactive educational game that turns learning about space into a fun journey for all ages, especially children.

Our idea started with a simple question: Where does space equipment go after missions end? We found that a lot of it is forgotten or left unused, so we decided instead of wasting it, to use it to sponsor people and inspire the next generation.

We developed a game where the player chooses a planet, completes fun missions, collects stars, and learns real scientific facts about planets and astronauts.

The importance of our project is that it makes learning through playing, not memorizing. It brings space science closer to every child, and turns forgotten equipment into an educational opportunity that creates hope, curiosity, and love for discovery.
details: Our project, Space Journey, started when we asked: Where does space equipment go after missions end? We found that a lot of equipment is forgotten, stored, or wasted. Our solution was to reuse this idea to sponsor people: to turn forgotten equipment into a tool to teach and inspire. We developed an educational game for everyone, especially children. The player starts as a young astronaut. In each level, the player travels to a new planet: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn. Each planet has fun missions, questions, and challenges. Our methodology was simple: 1. Research: We studied real facts about planets and astronauts from NASA open data. 2. Design: We designed characters, planets, and levels to be colorful and easy for kids. 3. Build: We created a prototype of the game with interactive levels, stars, points, and rewards. 4. Test: We tested the idea with children to see if they learn and enjoy it. The tools we used are Figma and Canva for design, and we made a demo prototype to show how the game works. The creative side is that learning becomes a journey, not a lesson. The player learns by playing, collecting stars, and finishing missions. We considered important factors: The game must be safe for kids, easy to use, educational, fun for all ages, and available for everyone, even without expensive equipment. Our result is a game that makes space education fun, turns waste into hope, and helps children love science and discovery.
